The evidence explicitly states that standard shadow maps store the depth to the nearest object, whereas deep shadow maps store volume density information as a function of distance (a curve representing transmission through the volume). This aligns with the claim that deep shadow maps capture volumetric structure along the light ray, unlike standard shadow maps which only capture the nearest surface.

Deep Shadow Maps are a shadow mapping technique for volume rendering where each pixel stores a curve representing volume density as a function of distance, rather than just the depth to the nearest opaque object [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Deep Shadow Maps are a technique for volume rendering where each pixel stores a curve of volume density as a function of distance, rather than just depth to the nearest opaque object. Source [S1] explicitly confirms this by stating: 'rather than storing the depth from the light to the nearest object... deep shadow maps store the density of the volume instead as a function of distance. In other words, each pixel in the deep shadow maps stores a curve that represents how transmission through the volume changes as we move through it.' All factual components of the claim are present and consistent with the evidence.
